{{notability|date=March 2023}}

{{nihongo|'''Jikkō kyō'''|実行教}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] organization<ref>{{Cite web |title=Japanese Meaning of 実行教, じっこうきょう, jikkōkyō |url=https://www.nihongomaster.com/japanese/dictionary/word/118012/jikkoukyou-%E5%AE%9F%E8%A1%8C%E6%95%99-%E3%81%98%E3%81%A3%E3%81%93%E3%81%86%E3%81%8D%E3%82%87%E3%81%86 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Nihongo Master |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> and one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=sn:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

It had a very complex institutional history having been formed in the {{ill|16th century|en|16th century|qid=Q7017|lt=16th century}} by {{ill|Hasegawa Kakugyo|en|Hasegawa Kakugyo|qid=Q11630860|lt=Hasegawa Kakugyo}} (who was also associated with [[Fuso-kyo]]) and eventually moved to support the Meiji government<ref>{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xlG3F6gSm9UC&dq=Jikk%C5%8D+ky%C5%8D&pg=PA131 |title=Historical Dictionary of Shinto |date=2010-12-28 |publisher=Scarecrow Press |isbn=978-0-8108-7372-8 |language=en}}</ref>

It is considered a "{{ill|Mountain worship|en|Mountain worship|qid=Q93697439|lt=Mountain worship}} sect" alongside [[Fuso-kyo]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shintō - Shintō reaction against Buddhism {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Shinto/Shinto-reaction-against-Buddhism |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=History of Art: Visual History of the World- Shinto |url=http://www.all-art.org/Visual_History/21-5.htm |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=www.all-art.org}}</ref> and {{ill|Ontake-kyō|en|Ontake-kyō|qid=Q6880734|lt=Ontakekyō}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=What is sectarian Shinto? - The Handy Religion Answer Book |url=https://www.papertrell.com/apps/preview/The-Handy-Religion-Answer-Book/Handy%20Answer%20book/What-is-sectarian-Shinto/001137024/content/SC/52cb017682fad14abfa5c2e0_default.html |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=www.papertrell.com}}</ref>

The official legal name uses the traditional characters (實行教), but many affiliated religious corporations are registered under the modern spelling (実行教).

== Overview ==

Jikkōkyō was founded by {{ill|Shibata Hanamori|ja|柴田花守|qid=Q134509164}} (also known as Sakyuki) in {{ill|1878|ab|1878|af|1878|als|1878|am|1878 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1878|ar|1878|ary|1878|arz|1878|ast|1878|avk|1878|az|1878|azb|۱۸۷۸ (میلادی)|ba|1878 йыл|ban|1878|bar|1878|bat_smg|1878|bcl|1878|be|1878|be_x_old|1878|bg|1878|bn|১৮৭৮|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৮|br|1878|bs|1878.|ca|1878|cdo|1878 nièng|ce|1878 шо|ceb|1878|ckb|١٨٧٨|crh|1878|cs|1878|csb|1878|cv|1878|cy|1878|da|1878|de|1878|diq|1878|el|1878|eml|1878|eo|1878|es|1878|et|1878|eu|1878|fa|۱۸۷۸|fi|1878|fiu_vro|1878|fo|1878|fr|1878|frp|1878|frr|1878|fur|1878|fy|1878|ga|1878|gan|1878年|gcr|1878|gd|1878|gl|1878|gn|1878|gv|1878|he|1878|hi|१८७८|hif|1878|hr|1878.|hsb|1878|ht|1878 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1878|hy|1878|hyw|1878 թուական|ia|1878|id|1878|ilo|1878|io|1878|is|1878|it|1878|ja|1878年|jv|1878|ka|1878|kaa|1878|kk|1878 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೮|ko|1878년|krc|1878 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1878|ku|1878|kv|1878-ӧд во|la|1878|lb|1878|lez|1878 йис|li|1878|lij|1878|lmo|1878|lt|1878 m.|lv|1878. gads|mai|१८७८|map_bms|1878|mdf|1878|mg|1878|mhr|1878|mi|1878|min|1878|mk|1878|ml|1878|mn|1878 он|mr|इ.स. १८७८|mrj|1878 и|ms|1878|my|၁၈၇၈|myv|1878 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۸|nah|1878|nap|1878|nds|1878|new|ई सं १८७८|nl|1878|nn|1878|no|1878|nrm|1878|nso|1878|oc|1878|olo|1878|or|୧୮୭୮|os|1878-æм аз|pa|1878|pap|1878|pl|1878|pnb|1878|pt|1878|qu|1878|ro|1878|roa_rup|1878|ru|1878 год|rue|1878|sa|१८७८|sah|1878|scn|1878|sd|1878ع|se|1878|sh|1878.|shn|1878|simple|1878|sk|1878|sl|1878|smn|1878|sq|1878|sr|1878|stq|1878|su|1878|sv|1878|sw|1878|szl|1878|ta|1878|te|1878|tg|Соли 1878|th|พ.ศ. 2421|tk|1878|tl|1878|tly|1878|tr|1878|tt|1878 ел|udm|1878 ар|uk|1878|ur|1878ء|uz|1878|vec|1878|vi|1878|vls|1878|vo|1878|wa|1878|war|1878|wuu|1878年|xmf|1878|yi|1878|za|1878 nienz|zea|1878|zh|1878年|zh_classical|一八七八年|zh_min_nan|1878 nî|zh_yue|1878年|qid=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) as "Jikkōsha" (実行社). It became an independent sect of {{ill|Sect Shinto|de|Sekten-Shintō|fr|Sectes Shinto|id|Sekte Shinto|ja|教派神道|ko|교파신토|lv|Sektu sintoisms|pl|Shintō sekciarskie|ru|Кёха синто|simple|Sect Shinto|zh|教派神道|qid=Q1532150|lt=Kōha Shintō}} in {{ill|1882|ab|1882|af|1882|als|1882|am|1882 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1882|ar|1882|ary|1882|arz|1882|ast|1882|avk|1882|az|1882|azb|۱۸۸۲ (میلادی)|ba|1882 йыл|ban|1882|bar|1882|bat_smg|1882|bcl|1882|be|1882|be_x_old|1882|bg|1882|bn|১৮৮২|bpy|মারি ১৮৮২|br|1882|bs|1882.|ca|1882|cdo|1882 nièng|ce|1882 шо|ceb|1882|ckb|١٨٨٢|crh|1882|cs|1882|csb|1882|cv|1882|cy|1882|da|1882|de|1882|diq|1882|el|1882|eml|1882|eo|1882|es|1882|et|1882|eu|1882|fa|۱۸۸۲|fi|1882|fiu_vro|1882|fo|1882|fr|1882|frp|1882|frr|1882|fur|1882|fy|1882|ga|1882|gan|1882年|gcr|1882|gd|1882|gl|1882|gv|1882|hak|1882-ngièn|he|1882|hi|१८८२|hif|1882|hr|1882.|hsb|1882|ht|1882 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1882|hy|1882|hyw|1882 թուական|ia|1882|id|1882|ilo|1882|io|1882|is|1882|it|1882|ja|1882年|jbo|1882moi|jv|1882|ka|1882|kaa|1882|kk|1882 жыл|kn|೧೮೮೨|ko|1882년|krc|1882 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1882|ku|1882|kv|1882-ӧд во|la|1882|lb|1882|lez|1882 йис|li|1882|lij|1882|lmo|1882|lt|1882 m.|lv|1882. gads|mai|१८८२|map_bms|1882|mdf|1882|mg|1882|mhr|1882|mi|1882|min|1882|mk|1882|ml|1882|mn|1882 он|mr|इ.स. १८८२|mrj|1882 и|ms|1882|my|၁၈၈၂|myv|1882 ие|mzn|۱۸۸۲|nah|1882|nap|1882|nds|1882|nds_nl|1882|new|ई सं १८८२|nl|1882|nn|1882|no|1882|nrm|1882|nso|1882|oc|1882|olo|1882|or|୧୮୮୨|os|1882-æм аз|pa|1882|pap|1882|pl|1882|pnb|1882|pt|1882|qu|1882|ro|1882|ru|1882 год|rue|1882|sa|१८८२|sah|1882|scn|1882|sd|1882ع|se|1882|sh|1882.|shn|1882|simple|1882|sk|1882|sl|1882|smn|1882|sq|1882|sr|1882|stq|1882|su|1882|sv|1882|sw|1882|szl|1882|ta|1882|te|1882|tg|Соли 1882|th|พ.ศ. 2425|tk|1882|tl|1882|tly|1882|tr|1882|tt|1882 ел|udm|1882 ар|ug|1882 - يىلى|uk|1882|ur|1882ء|uz|1882|vec|1882|vi|1882|vls|1882|vo|1882|wa|1882|war|1882|xmf|1882|yi|1882|za|1882 nienz|zea|1882|zh|1882年|zh_classical|一八八二年|zh_min_nan|1882 nî|zh_yue|1882年|qid=Q7812|lt=1882}} (Meiji 15) and was officially recognized as "Jikkōkyō"{{sfn|Inoue Nobutaka et al.|1996|p=98}}.

Like {{ill|Fuso-kyo|ja|扶桑教|qid=Q11497295}}, Jikkōkyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Hasegawa Kakugyo|ja|長谷川角行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasegawa Kakugyō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 角行 (富士講)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11630860}}, the founder of the Fuji faith. It follows the branch of {{ill|Itō Miroku|ja|伊藤身禄}}, also known as {{ill|Jikigyō Miroku|ja|食行身禄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugyō Miroku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11666087}}
{{sfn|Inoue Nobutaka|1991|p=17}}.

Jikkōkyō descends through:
- '''Fifth-generation leader''' {{ill|Jikigyō Miroku|ja|食行身禄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugyō Miroku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11666087}}
- '''Sixth-generation leader''' {{ill|Itō Ikko|ja|伊藤一行}}, the third daughter of Miroku
- '''Seventh-generation leader''' {{ill|Itō Sango|ja|伊藤参行}}, Ikko’s adopted son

{{ill|Itō Sango|ja|伊藤参行}} attracted disciples, including {{ill|Sanshi Otani|ja|小谷三志|qid=Q17209484}}, who expanded the sect{{sfn|Inoue Nobutaka|1991|p=17}}. In {{ill|1838|en|1838|qid=Q7612|lt=1838}} (Tenpō 9), the sect was renamed '''Fujidō''' (不二道){{sfn|Inoue Nobutaka|1991|p=18}}. 

Two major branches emerged:
1. '''Fusōkyō''' (spread by the Shishino family)
2. '''Jikkōkyō''' (spread by the Shibata family)<ref>[https://books.google.co.jp/books?id=3418dDYaP3IC&pg=PA190　 『国家に及ぼす宗教の害毒』日高瓊々彦、大同館書店, 1928]</ref>

Jikkōkyō emphasizes '''practical action and discipline''' over Fuji faith’s esoteric aspects{{sfn|Sugata|1985|p=167}}. Members receive '''a spiritual name''' upon initiation, indicating their training path, and later, '''three titles of achievement''' upon reaching higher spiritual progress.
